as_told.title: Brandenburg: argon-40 and xenon-129 show a nuclear cataclysm on Mars

plain: The claim is that Mars was once home to a civilisation wiped out by nuclear war, and that the proof lies in the Martian air: far more of two gases, xenon-129 and argon-40, than natural radioactive decay should produce. The plasma physicist and propulsion scientist John Brandenburg tells Michels this himself. He says NASA's Viking missions measured the gases in 1976 and found "a large amount of xenon 129," which comes from only two things, "supernova explosions and hydrogen bomb explosions," and "we know there was no supernova on Mars." He recalls the moment it all came together in his office: "I wept like a child for about 4 minutes. Why? Cuz they were all dead." He places that realisation in the 1980s, while others place his work in the 2010s. The philosopher Jason Jorjani says he spent several days with Brandenburg in New Mexico and wrote up the research, tied to the Martian region called Cydonia, in his book Closer Encounters. Michels repeats it on several episodes, once crediting an unnamed friend who worked at the national weapons labs Lawrence Livermore and Sandia, and John Blitch, a former DARPA scientist, mentions it in passing as Brandenburg's speculation. If true, it would mean intelligent life arose on another planet and destroyed itself.
